title: Native project directory selection bridge
objective: Add one native Tauri command, select_project_directory, that opens the OS directory dialog in Rust, lets the user choose a directory, and returns the chosen directory path (Ok(Some(path)) on selection, Ok(None) when the dialog is dismissed). The command accepts ZERO caller-supplied filesystem arguments: a caller cannot pass path, directory or project_path - Rust obtains the selection from the OS dialog itself. This does not weaken the renderer boundary, because a CAN-X project path is already the explicit input of the Runtime's GET /project/inspect contract. Rust must NOT validate that the selection is a CAN-X project: no reading project.json, no opening project.db, no schema check, no project-identity check, no copy of ProjectService logic. Project authority stays with the Python Runtime ProjectService; this bridge owns only the user filesystem selection. Errors are typed, static and bounded, and never echo the selected path. Reuse the existing tauri_plugin_dialog directory picker; add no dependency and do not modify Cargo.toml.
scope: The new Rust project-directory bridge module, its tests, the lib.rs command registration, and the DBC bridge's registered-command-surface regression test that the new registration invalidates.
non_goals: Any project validation, project identity check or ProjectService logic in Rust
Reading project.json, opening project.db or checking a schema from Rust
Any new crate dependency, any Cargo.toml / Cargo.lock change
Any renderer capability change, any TypeScript change and any Runtime change
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one new command is registered, named select_project_directory, and its only argument is the Tauri-injected AppHandle - no caller-supplied filesystem argument exists

The registered command surface regression in dbc_file_bridge/tests.rs is updated to the new reviewed surface AND its parameter scan is extended to project_directory_bridge.rs with its inspected-command count raised accordingly - the invariant is preserved, not weakened
Cancel resolves to Ok(None) and selection resolves to Ok(Some(directory path)); the bridge performs no project validation of the selection
Every failure is a declared typed code with static message text, and no published payload or error contains the selected directory path
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked all pass
handoff_requirements: Report the exact command and result for cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked, run from apps/desktop/src-tauri
Name every new test case and state the RED observation that preceded each new behaviour, including the command-surface regression that the new registration turned red
State explicitly that Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and capabilities/default.json were not modified, and that no project-validation logic was added to Rust
